findings.title: float: right on .small-action button is dead because the container is now flexbox
findings.body: This PR makes .small-action a flex container (@include flexbox() at the top of the rule), but the nested button still relies on `float: right` for its position. The float property has no effect on flex items, so the button rendered in small-action posts (e.g. the staff edit/action button on 'topic closed'-style posts) will no longer be pinned to the right edge of the row — it will be laid out immediately after .small-action-desc, because neither the button nor .small-action-desc has margin-left: auto or flex-grow to push it right. Add `margin-left: auto` to the button (or let .small-action-desc grow) and remove the now-inert float.

findings.title: margin-left: auto used to right-align .panel does not work in the legacy box syntax the flexbox() mixin emits
findings.body: .panel lost `float: right` and is now pushed to the right edge solely by `margin-left: auto` inside the flex container .contents. The flexbox() mixin applied to .contents also emits the 2009-syntax `display: -webkit-box` / `display: -moz-box` fallbacks, and the 2009 flexbox model does not support auto margins (they compute to 0). So in exactly the legacy browsers those prefixes exist for, the header icon panel will sit immediately after the title instead of at the right edge — a regression from the previous float-based layout, which worked everywhere. Either drop the 2009 display fallbacks or provide a fallback (e.g. keep a float on .panel, or use -webkit-box-pack on the container).

findings.title: align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align, inconsistent with the other new flexbox mixins
findings.body: The new align-items mixin emits -webkit-box-align, -ms-flex-align and modern declarations but no -moz-box-align. Its sibling mixins flexbox() and order() both include the 2009 Mozilla syntax (-moz-box, -moz-box-ordinal-group), so on Gecko versions that only implement the legacy box model, an element using these mixins becomes a -moz-box with ordering applied while the requested alignment (center in the header/small-action, baseline on category bullets) is silently ignored — the mixin half-works in exactly the engines it claims to support. Add `-moz-box-align: $alignment;` for consistency (the 2009 spec accepts start/end/center/baseline/stretch).
